article.title: Why a High Conversion Rate Can Be Misleading When Eligibility Changes
article.why: Practical analytical English for data-driven decisions.

paragraphs.en: Conversion rate looks simple: divide conversions by the number of eligible or contacted customers. The difficulty is that the denominator can change. If eligibility rules become stricter, a campaign may exclude low-propensity customers before delivery. The measured conversion rate can then rise even when the treatment itself has not improved. Imagine that last year a campaign could reach one million customers, including many inactive accounts. This year a new negative check removes inactive accounts, customers without valid consent, and people who cannot receive the channel. Only six hundred thousand remain. If most removed customers were unlikely to convert, the new eligible population has a higher baseline probability. Comparing the two conversion rates directly mixes a population change with a campaign effect. Channel restrictions can create the same problem. Email, push notification, direct mail, and outbound calling have different eligibility conditions. A move from one channel to another can alter who enters the denominator. Even a model refresh can change the selected population if the campaign contacts only customers above a score threshold. Analysts should therefore define the funnel explicitly: source population, eligibility checks, targetable population, assigned population, delivered population, and outcome population. Rates calculated at different stages answer different questions. A delivery conversion rate may be useful for operational performance, while an intent-to-treat rate may be more appropriate for causal evaluation. Cross-period comparisons should either hold the population definition constant or quantify how much of the change comes from composition. Standardization, reweighting, or a common eligibility filter can help. The language of the conclusion matters as well. “Conversion among eligible customers increased” is narrower and more defensible than “the campaign became more effective.” The second statement requires evidence that treatment effectiveness changed rather than merely the denominator. A high rate is informative only when the population behind that rate is understood. Before celebrating a percentage, ask who was allowed into the denominator, who was removed, and whether those rules changed over time. Analysts should document the population, observation window, assumptions, and operational definition before drawing a conclusion. A useful review separates the observed metric from the mechanism that may have produced it and from the action that should follow. This discipline makes the result easier to reproduce, challenge, and communicate to stakeholders. paragraphs.zh: 繁中完整翻譯與解說：本文的核心不是只看表面指標，而是先確認母體、分母、時間範圍與選擇機制，再判斷數字是否真的代表 business outcome 改善。分析時要區分觀察事實、可能機制與因果結論，並把不確定性、經濟價值與下一步 action 一起納入。
paragraphs.ja: 日本語完全訳・解説：表面的なmetricだけで結論を出さず、母集団、分母、期間、selection mechanismを確認したうえでbusiness outcomeの改善を判断する。観察事実、考えられるmechanism、因果的な結論を分け、不確実性、経済価値、次のactionまで含めて説明することが重要である。
